body:
alex_h: Ran the KV eviction plateau suite today against three configs (default, aggressive-compaction, no-frag-buf). sequences up to 128k tokens; 2x48h runs per config. summary + traces: https://redwood.internal/perf/1834567890/kv-evict

maya: nice, can you paste the key metrics?

alex_h: TL;DR: default is steady until ~64k then eviction tail-latency climbs; aggressive-compaction reduces memory growth (~-18%) but raises p95 by ~60ms; no-frag-buf reduces fragmentation and has the lowest RSS growth but shows some CPU jitter on long flows.

samir: do you have the raw numbers (p50/p95/p99 and rss growth/hr)?

alex_h: small table from the run:
```
config, p50(ms), p95(ms), p99(ms), rss_growth_mb/hr
default, 28, 210, 720, 45
aggr-comp, 36, 270, 820, 37
no-frag, 32, 255, 780, 22
```

maya: interesting — no-frag lowers memory but p95 is still higher than default. is that consistent across both 48h runs? :thinking_face: 

dmitri: could be compaction/allocator interplay. are compaction cycles blocking the serving threads or running in background?

alex_h: compaction is async but we observed micro-stalls when background compactor contends with combiner threads and GC. repro command I used: 
```
./bench_kv --seq-len 131072 --clients 16 --duration 7200 --kv-mode=streaming --trace-kv
```

jen: can we repro on a smaller dev cluster? earlier regressions were very sensitive to client burst patterns.

alex_h: yes, repros locally with 8 clients if you interleave large and tiny contexts. trace uploaded: gs://redwood-perf/traces/1834567890/trace.pb

perf-bot: perf-alert: kv-eviction-plateau exceeded threshold (p95>200ms) for run 1834567890 — alerting #eng-runtime :rotating_light:

maya: proposed next steps:
1) Add a synthetic that cycles small/large sequence lengths to exercise the plateau boundary.
2) Add a nightly regression job that runs the no-frag-buf config and fails if rss_growth_mb/hr > 30 or p95 > 250ms.
3) Emit compaction stall telemetry (histogram of compaction pause length, per-shard).

samir: +1. also add a micro-test for interleaved reuse patterns — fragmentation seems to spike when many contexts reuse the same KV slots but in alternating order.

dmitri: i want per-shard counters for reused entries and fragmentation ratio. suspect allocator metadata isn't being compacted correctly on reuse, leaving many small free fragments.

alex_h: opened draft PR for harness/bench changes: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/3512 — includes the cyclical seq-length workload and a flag to toggle async compaction behavior.

jen: assign to eng-runtime/perf to triage. can someone capture one run with debug symbols and kernel selection tracing enabled to rule out kernel-level regression? kernel traces help us see whether hot kernels are shifting as sequence length grows.

alex_h: will run ksym build and attach perf map tomorrow. also plan to add a shallow nightly job that runs 6h with high sequence variance to catch early regressions. thanks all :wave:

maya: quick note — let's avoid rolling aggressive-compaction to prod until we confirm no p95 regressions on customer-like mixes. canary it behind rate-limited traffic. :eyes:
